voices.original_text: Two laptops, one network: 192.168.1.20 and 192.168.1.50. Add /24. What does it mean?
voices.spoken_text: Two laptops, one network: one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot one dot twenty and one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot one dot fifty. Add slash 24. What does it mean?

voices.original_text: An IP address is really 32 bits, written as four groups called octets. Eight bits, eight bits, eight bits, eight bits.
voices.spoken_text: An I P address is really 32 bits, written as four groups called octets. Eight bits, eight bits, eight bits, eight bits.

voices.original_text: /24 says the first 24 bits describe the network. So the first three octets name the network, and the last octet is left for hosts.
voices.spoken_text: slash 24 says the first 24 bits describe the network. So the first three octets name the network, and the last octet is left for hosts.

voices.original_text: That same boundary has a second name: the subnet mask. /24 and 255.255.255.0 are the same divide.
voices.spoken_text: That same boundary has a second name: the subnet mask. slash 24 and two fifty five dot two fifty five dot two fifty five dot zero are the same divide.

voices.original_text: Set every host bit to zero, and you get the network address: the name of this subnet.
voices.spoken_text: Set every host bit to zero, and you get the network address: the name of this subnet.

voices.original_text: Inside the subnet, addresses run from dot zero to dot two fifty five. The last one, all host bits set, is the broadcast address.
voices.spoken_text: Inside the subnet, addresses run from dot zero to dot two fifty five. The last one, all host bits set, is the broadcast address.

voices.original_text: Reserve those two, and 254 addresses are left for devices. Here: a router, a laptop, a phone, and a server.
voices.spoken_text: Reserve those two, and 254 addresses are left for devices. Here: a router, a laptop, a phone, and a server.

voices.original_text: Both laptops now. Same first 24 bits, so they reach each other through the switch.
voices.spoken_text: Both laptops now. Same first 24 bits, so they reach each other through the switch.

voices.original_text: Move one laptop to 192.168.2.50, and the network portions stop matching. Different subnets.
voices.spoken_text: Move one laptop to one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot two dot fifty, and the network portions stop matching. Different subnets.

voices.original_text: That destination is not local, so the laptop sends it to its default gateway, the router at dot one.
voices.spoken_text: That destination is not local, so the laptop sends it to its default gateway, the router at dot one.

voices.original_text: Zoom out: two subnets, one router. Every device asks one simple question: is the destination local, or does it go to the router?
voices.spoken_text: Zoom out: two subnets, one router. Every device asks one simple question: is the destination local, or does it go to the router?

voices.original_text: So /24 means the first 24 bits name the network, and the last 8 address the devices inside it. Same subnet, local. Different subnet, the router. Next: a switch, or a router?
